Here is a budget plan for Derrick’s transition from renting to owning rock climbing gear. Note that prices are estimates based on average market rates for mid-to-high quality recreational gear. Prices can vary significantly based on brand, new vs. used condition, and specific technical requirements.

### **Initial Purchase Budget (One-Time Costs)**

| Item | Estimated Cost Range (USD) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Climbing Shoes** | $80 – $150 | Entry-level to mid-range. Essential for performance and comfort. |
| **Harness** | $60 – $120 | Look for adjustable leg loops and gear loops. |
| **Helmet** | $50 – $100 | CE/UIAA certified. Protects against falling debris and impact. |
| **Carabiners (Set of 6-8)** | $60 – $120 | Quickdraws (2 carabiners + sling) are needed for top-roping/bouldering. Assume 6-8 carabiners for basic setup. |
| **Rope (60m Dynamic)** | $150 – $250 | 9.8mm–10.2mm diameter is standard for gym and outdoor top-roping. |
| **Belay Device** | $20 – $40 | ATC or assisted-braking device (e.g., Grigri). |
| **Chalk Bag & Chalk** | $15 – $30 | Optional but highly recommended for grip. |
| **Total Initial Cost** | **$435 – $810** | **Average: ~$620** |

> **Tip:** Derrick can reduce initial costs by buying used gear (especially shoes, harness, and helmet if not expired) from reputable sources or climbing gyms. However, ropes and harnesses have a lifespan and should be inspected carefully if bought used.
